title: Discord Community Guidelines (effective 29 September 2025, last updated 29 August 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Age-restricted channel labels, bans on spam, self-bots and user-bots, artificially inflating membership or engagement, buying or selling servers, ban evasion; reports from users and moderators; Discord's range of enforcement actions.

title: Discord Terms of Service (effective 29 September 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Server owners and admins control permissions and extra rules but must follow Discord's policies; users are responsible for what they post; Discord may remove content and suspend accounts; enforcement can be appealed.

title: Role of administrators and moderators on Discord (12 May 2022)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. What admins and moderators do, and the advice that each server writes its own behaviour rules on top of Discord's guidelines.

title: How we enforce our rules (12 May 2022)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Discord's own actions against users and servers, including blocking a server from inviting new members and removing a server.

title: New anti-spam, raid and AutoMod safety update (21 September 2022)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. AutoMod spam and mention-spam filters, the suspicious link filter on Community servers, Pause Invites and raid reports. Dated 2022; check current settings in the app.

title: Feature limitations on the free version of Slack
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page undated). Free plan: 90 days of message and file access, content older than one year deleted, 10 integrations, one-to-one huddles.

title: Deactivate a member's account
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page undated). Who can deactivate; the person is not notified; messages and files are kept; deactivation can be reversed; available on all plans.

title: Slack MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page undated). Slack publishes an official MCP server for search, reading and sending messages; workspace admins approve and manage MCP clients.

title: Get to know content moderation (updated 30 June 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Reporting, a report threshold that hides content, automatic flagging (profanity filter, flagged members), the Reports queue, approve or reject, and reversible decisions.

title: Explore the capabilities of a moderator (updated 18 December 2022)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Moderators act only in assigned spaces; settings, analytics and billing stay with admins; space moderators can add and remove members in their spaces.

title: Deactivate, delete, or ban members (updated October 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Differences between deactivate (reversible, content stays), delete (permanent erase) and ban (permanent erase, IP block, lifting needs Circle support); members are not notified; actions appear in activity logs.

title: Get to know the Circle MCP (updated October 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Circle MCP: admins only, Business plan and higher, read-only or full access chosen at sign-in, OAuth connection, request limits.

title: Manage people and content (Facebook Groups)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page undated). Group admin tools: Admin Assist, membership questions, preapprovals, tagging a rule in a post or comment, remove, ban, suspend and limit members.

title: Digital Services Act: questions and answers (last updated 19 December 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. DSA applies to all regulated services from 17 February 2024; easy reporting of illegal content, prompt handling, telling both sides; statements of reasons; free internal complaints handled by qualified staff; out-of-court dispute settlement; lighter rules for small and micro firms.

title: The Digital Services Act (policy page, last updated 1 October 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Platforms must explain removals, let users appeal, offer easy reporting, and avoid deceptive dark-pattern designs; micro and small companies have lighter requirements.

title: Online Safety Act: explainer (updated 24 April 2025)
publisher: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Which services are in scope (including forums and small services, proportionately), key dates (illegal content duties from 17 March 2025; children's risk assessments by 24 July 2025), duties, and Ofcom fines.

title: 47 U.S. Code § 230: Protection for private blocking and screening of offensive material
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Text of Section 230(c)(1), (c)(2) good-faith removal, and the exceptions in 230(e).

title: Section 512 of Title 17: Resources on online service provider safe harbors and notice-and-takedown system
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Notice-and-takedown, counter-notices and the 10 to 14 business-day restore window, the designated agent and its three-year renewal, repeat-infringer policy.

title: The Santa Clara Principles on Transparency and Accountability in Content Moderation (2.0, 2021)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Understandable rules, notice of what was actioned and why, appeal reviewed by someone not involved, telling users when automation is used.

title: The 90-9-1 Rule for Participation Inequality in Social Media and Online Communities (Jakob Nielsen, 8 October 2006)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 90-9-1 pattern, its caveats, and ways to shape participation (lower barriers, reward moderately, promote quality).

title: The Beginners' Guide To Community Management
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated; FeverBee founder Richard Millington named as contact). Four layers of a community (common interest, means of engagement, relationships, purpose); the community manager as host rather than broadcaster; daily tasks.

title: Proving Community ROI
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). Value framework: lifetime value, acquisition, cost reduction, efficiency and social return against technology, staff and process costs.

title: 2026 CMX Community Industry Report
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Seventh annual report; lean teams, diverging budgets, lower confidence in proving ROI, 93% of community professionals using AI tools, up from 81% the year before.

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Opened with WebFetch (Guides revised 2023). Employees and owners disclose their connection in each post; disclosures sit in the endorsement itself; #ambassador alone is not enough; brands train and monitor ambassador programmes.

title: Negative Option Rule
